dataset: Volcanoes of the World (VOTW) – Holocene volcano list (WFS)
description: Reference list of the roughly 1,200 volcanoes known or thought to have erupted during the Holocene (the past ~12,000 years), with volcano type, last known eruption year, elevation, tectonic setting and evidence category.

coverage.temporal: Reference data: volcanoes with Holocene activity; the last-eruption year reflects the current database version.

updateCadence.upstream: Database versions are released a few times a year (VOTW 5.x)

attribution: Global Volcanism Program, Smithsonian Institution – Volcanoes of the World (https://doi.org/10.5479/si.GVP.VOTW5-2026.5.4)

license.name: Smithsonian Institution Terms of Use – usage conditions apply (non-commercial use; cite GVP Volcanoes of the World)
license.notes: The WFS capabilities document states Fees: NONE and AccessConstraints: NONE but no licence. Smithsonian content that is not marked CC0 may be used for personal, educational and other non-commercial purposes; commercial use needs prior permission. GVP asks for the citation 'Global Volcanism Program, 2026. [Database] Volcanoes of the World (v. 5.4.0). Distributed by Smithsonian Institution, compiled by Venzke, E.' The Smithsonian documentation and terms pages are behind a browser verification challenge and could not be read directly when this adapter was written; this entry rests on search-engine excerpts of those pages and should be re-checked by a human before any commercial use. To stay conservative the adapter requests facts only (no geological summaries, photos or captions) and links to the GVP volcano page.

limitations: A reference catalogue, not a monitoring feed: it does not say whether a volcano is erupting now (see the weekly volcanic activity layer).
Last-eruption years are those of the current database version; negative years are BCE and many volcanoes have no dated eruption.
A single summit coordinate represents each volcano, including large volcanic fields and calderas.
The evidence category ranges from observed eruptions to uncertain evidence of Holocene activity.
confidenceNotes: No confidence value is assigned. GVP's own 'evidence category' (Eruption Observed, Eruption Dated, Evidence Credible, Evidence Uncertain, Unrest / Holocene) is kept verbatim as an attribute. No severity: this is reference data.

retention.note: Reference data: kept while the volcano is listed upstream; replaced on every successful weekly fetch.

layers.name: Holocene volcanoes (GVP)
layers.description: Volcanoes active in the past ~12,000 years from the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, with type and last known eruption.
